# Website maintenance

**Canonical address:** [https://awesomerea.org](https://awesomerea.org). The display name is **AwesomeREA.org**. Search metadata uses one site name, **Awesome Reverse Engineering Anything**, with `AwesomeREA.org` and `Awesome REA` as alternate names in that order.

## Source and generated files

- [site/](../site/) contains the dependency-free HTML, CSS, JavaScript, favicon and social image. Update the SVG and PNG together when the illustration changes. The pages follow the reader's system color scheme: styles.css declares `color-scheme: light dark`, defines every palette color as a `:root` token and restates each token under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` (papers.css and survey.css do the same for their own few colors). Use a token rather than a literal color in new rules, and use `--on-ink` for text on ink-filled controls, which turn light in the dark theme. Every page carries a light and a dark `theme-color` from `THEME_COLOR_META` in open_graph.py.
- [open_graph.py](../scripts/open_graph.py) writes the Open Graph and Twitter card tags for the homepage and every generated page, with `og:site_name` set to its `SITE_NAME`, with the image type and size read from `social-card.png` and a localized description of the card as its alt text. Resource and paper detail pages are `og:type` `article`, every other page `website`; a page may pass its own card under `/og/` with a description of that card. The 404 pages have no `og:url`. The same module defines the WebSite node (`#website`): only the two homepages include it, and every other page's JSON-LD refers to it by `@id`. `validate_site.py` checks both against these constants.
- [site_footer.py](../scripts/site_footer.py) renders the footer every generated page shares: the seven sections (ending with Contribute), then the curated catalog, repository, paper metadata and BibTeX downloads, then GitHub. It also holds the one English and one Chinese name for each of those downloads, which hero buttons and `/about/` reuse. [index.html](../site/index.html) repeats the footer with `data-i18n` keys and adds the contributor links; `validate_site.py` fails when a page's footer differs or a download appears under a second name.
- [rea-resources.json](../data/rea-resources.json) and [tool-resources.json](../data/tool-resources.json) are the resource sources. Keep bilingual descriptions, evidence links, prerequisites, review dates and target labels accurate.
- [translations.zh-CN.json](../site/translations.zh-CN.json) supplies Chinese resource names and prerequisites. New records also need translations here.
- [topics.i18n.json](../site/topics.i18n.json) supplies bilingual display labels for common repository topics. Canonical upstream topic IDs remain intact for links and exact filtering.
- [source-index.json](../data/source-index.json) supplies the broader repository collection from successful automated README fetches. Its counts and review status stay separate from the curated records. [Repository locale files](../data/locales/README.md) provide English and Simplified Chinese descriptions; the generated data also preserves the original upstream text. See [scan methodology](source-scan.md).
- [source-scope.json](../data/source-scope.json) removes clearly unrelated scan matches, duplicate README copies and repositories whose upstream is no longer available from browsing while keeping their original scan evidence in the full downloadable JSON. The footer offers separate repository-index and curated-catalog downloads.
- [source_browser.py](../scripts/source_browser.py) generates compact `source-browser.json` for interactive search. It contains eligible records in the same order, with bilingual/original-text search, card details and evidence annotations. The full `/source-index.json` download remains complete, including excluded records, failures and discovery history. The browser payload records the full export's SHA-256 and is checked against it during the build. The interactive repository cards keep one complete set of related entries and topics in native details for either layout. Dates remain together, while full hashes, advertised Git revision, scan status and byte size sit under “README scan evidence”. Shared prerequisite advice lives in “About this index”; it does not imply individual review. The topic filter explains exact-ID versus text-containing matches without changing its URL or matching behavior.
- [build_production.py](../scripts/build_production.py) reads the current GitHub star counts of the repositories in `data/repository-stats.json`, without a token, before it runs `build_site.py` and the validators ([repository_stats.py](../scripts/repository_stats.py)). A failed read keeps the recorded number. `build_site.py` alone uses the recorded numbers.
- [build_site.py](../scripts/build_site.py) combines the catalogs, derives counts, copies the site assets, and generates `catalog.json`, the lean homepage index `catalog-index.json`, `robots.txt` (from the crawler list in [crawl_policy.py](../scripts/crawl_policy.py)), the `sitemap.xml` index with its four section sitemaps (from [sitemaps.py](../scripts/sitemaps.py), with data-derived `lastmod` dates and hreflang alternates), `CNAME` and `.nojekyll` in `dist/`. A page builder that adds a route returns its URL to the build, and `sitemaps.section_for` files it under pages, resources, papers or categories.
- [build_browse_pages.py](../scripts/build_browse_pages.py) emits 20 static category pages under `/browse/` and `/zh/browse/`. These include full localized repository content without JavaScript, reciprocal language links, canonical URLs, and sitemap entries. Each card shows the star count, last-push month and license recorded at collection time, labelled as snapshots without a maintenance judgement. Below 521 px the month appears without its visible “Last push” / “最近推送” label, which stays in its accessible name and tooltip, so the four items keep one row. Like the collection, paper and detail pages, each publishes a BreadcrumbList with the names and destinations of its visible breadcrumb; `validate_site.py` compares the two on every page. Counts and scope exclusions use the same data as search. Each category page's Search repositories link adds `source-category=<slug>`, which opens the homepage Repositories view with that category selected in its Category filter. The filter's labels come from `source_category_labels`, the same map the category pages use, which `catalog.json` and the lean `catalog-index.json` both carry, and it lists only categories the browsable records use. It combines with the query, target, topic and sort, shows as a removable chip, is restored by Back and Forward, is named among a repository export's filters, clears on its own or with Clear filters, and an unknown value falls back to all categories. Record classifications are not changed.
- [build_discovery_pages.py](../scripts/build_discovery_pages.py) emits bilingual `/resources/` and `/about/` pages, evidence and review dates for curated entries, structured metadata, and the optional `llms.txt` navigation index. The homepage and browse pages link to these pages; the “Collection notes” link under the homepage's curated filters opens the About page in the page's language. The `/resources/` and `/cases/` action rows link the existing resource and case-study issue forms, as `/papers/` links the paper form; `validate_site.py` checks all three in both languages. Each section heading row on `/resources/` and `/cases/` ends with an “All sections ↑” link (“全部分类 ↑” / “全部主题 ↑” in Chinese) back to the section chips above the first section. A `/resources/` section holding both case studies and other kinds lists them, in README order, under “Case studies” and “Tools, projects and integrations” sub-headings with their counts (`#<section>--case-studies`, `#<section>--tools`); card titles there are `h4` so heading levels do not skip, and `#<id>` card fragments are unchanged. It also writes the `noindex` 404 pages: `404.html` in English and `zh/404.html` in Chinese, which Cloudflare Pages serves for misses under `/zh/`. Each has a GET search form that sends `q` to its homepage's curated search, links to the main sections and a link to the other language's homepage.
- [build_survey.py](../scripts/build_survey.py) renders the bilingual editorial survey at `/survey/` and `/zh/survey/`, plus repository-citation and paper-reference BibTeX downloads. The Cite action uses the collection identity and author order from `CITATION.cff`, without inventing a repository release date or version; `/survey/citation.bib` remains the compatible download URL. [survey.json](../data/survey.json) freezes its corpus and cited source records independently of future catalog updates. The survey is not a research-paper record and does not increase the paper count. Update both languages, source evidence and version together when revising its argument; the homepage, README and `llms.txt` link to it.
- [build_entry_pages.py](../scripts/build_entry_pages.py) emits one English/Chinese detail-page pair for each curated resource and paper: `/resources/<id>/`, `/papers/<id>/` and their `/zh/` counterparts. These pages retain complete reviewed descriptions, requirements or research limits, original source links and citation metadata. They describe the catalog entry; they do not replace the upstream project or paper. A resource page also carries a “Copy as Markdown” link to its `index.md` twin (site.js copies the file; without the Clipboard API the link opens it), a “View JSON” link to `record.json`, a Cite section with BibTeX and plain text built from the record's name, URL, review date and entry address, and one star line for this repository after the citation. When `data/repository-metadata.json` holds the resource's GitHub repository, a row under the summary shows its stars, last default-branch commit, primary language and GitHub's detected license, dated by the snapshot; [repository_metadata.py](../scripts/repository_metadata.py) `--refresh` rewrites that snapshot with one GraphQL query per 50 repositories, and the build only reads it. Each page's review section links the resource-correction and translation-correction issue forms, prefilled with a `Correction:` or `Translation:` title from the record's English name and with the record ID in the form's `resource` field; `validate_site.py` checks both links on every detail page.
- Interactive cards offer a Copy link action next to their internal or README link. Homepage curated cards copy the entry page (`/resources/<id>/`), repository cards copy their card on the static category page (`/browse/<category>/#<id>`), and paper cards on `/papers/` copy `/papers/<id>/`, each in the page's language and on the canonical `awesomerea.org` origin. Only these fixed routes, built from IDs and categories that match the slug pattern, can be copied; title links still open the upstream resource. The button's accessible name includes the entry name, and a polite status confirms the copy. When the Clipboard API is unavailable or refused, a read-only field with the selected link appears beside the button for a manual copy.
- [build_feed.py](../scripts/build_feed.py) writes Atom feeds at `/feed.xml` and `/zh/feed.xml` with the 50 most recently added curated resources and papers by `added_at`, each linking its localized detail page. The feed date is the newest `added_at`, never the build time or a review date, so rebuilding a commit reproduces the feeds byte for byte. Each feed has a [JSON Feed 1.1](https://www.jsonfeed.org/version/1.1/) twin, `/feed.json` and `/zh/feed.json`, with the same items in the same order. Both homepages and the `/resources/`, `/cases/` and `/papers/` listings advertise their language's feeds with `<link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">` and `type="application/feed+json"`, and `site/_headers` serves them as `application/atom+xml` and `application/feed+json`. Without dated records no feed or link is written. `validate_site.py` binds every entry to its record and detail page.
- `/cases/` and `/zh/cases/` provide a compact subject index of the existing case-study records. The homepage's “Artifact reviews · Beta” entry opens this collection. Its visible review method separates reconstruction scope, available artifacts, evidence/attribution and runtime status; the current phase reviews documentation without independently certifying completeness or compatibility. Complete descriptions remain visible; each row shows its review date and links to the entry page's requirements and sources. The method and directory work without JavaScript. The Games section is grouped by `reconstruction_method`, with a method index, a one-sentence definition and a count per group, in the same groups and order as the README's Game case studies (`#cases-game-<method>`); cases without a method form a final “Other reconstruction methods” group (`#cases-game-unassigned`), shown only when it has entries.
- `/resources/` and `/cases/` file each entry once, under its primary section. Each target section (Website to Protocol) also states how many listed entries carry that target, names them when no more than nine are filed under other sections, and links the homepage filtered to that target (plus `kind=case-study` on `/cases/`), whose result count matches. Sections are assigned by category, so a section can also list entries without its tag; the line then adds “N listed here by category without the Website tag” (in Chinese, 另有 N 项按分类列于本节但不带“网站”标签), naming them when there are no more than nine. The section count is therefore always tagged, minus filed elsewhere, plus listed here without the tag. The line carries the three numbers as `data-target-tagged`, `data-target-elsewhere` and `data-target-untagged-here`; `validate_site.py` and the browser smoke test check that they match the catalog and add up to the section's cards.
- Static collection lists and related-entry links lead to these detail pages using ordinary links. On the README, homepage, `/resources/` and `/cases/`, an entry’s title opens the original resource and “Full entry” opens its detail page; `evidence_url` is labelled “Primary source” / “一手来源”. On `/resources/` and `/cases/` this source link sits beside a counted link such as “3 requirements · 2 sources” to the entry page's `#entry-requirements` section. The full requirement and source lists, with their facet and source labels, appear only on entry pages, which keeps the listing pages light; the homepage search still matches requirement text. The `/resources/` and `/cases/` structured lists identify each item by its localized detail page, while visible resource card titles still link upstream. The `/papers/` ItemList gives each paper's entry-page URL, localized title, position and the `@id` of the `ScholarlyArticle` that only the entry page describes. Existing `/resources/#<id>` and `/papers/#<id>` listing anchors remain available; the card that a fragment targets on `/resources/`, `/cases/` or `/papers/` is tinted and outlined, with a system-color outline in forced-colors mode. On the homepage, ↗ marks only links that leave awesomerea.org and open a new tab; links to the site's own pages and data files use → or no glyph. Linked titles on `/resources/`, `/cases/`, the `/browse/` category pages and the homepage repository view keep their trailing ↗ or external-link icon on the line of the title's last character. Each resource page in a README section with other entries ends with a "More in <section>" block: up to six following entries of that section in README order (case studies first, wrapping to the section start), a link to the section heading on `/resources/` and, for case studies, to the case section on `/cases/`. `validate_site.py` recomputes the list for every page. The paper directory defaults to a compact list, including without JavaScript. On phones (600 px and narrower) the search field keeps the full width, Target sits beside “More filters” (which holds Publication status, Year, Layout and the search help, and opens by itself when one of them is set), the result count sits beside “Clear filters”, and the research-area links scroll sideways in one row, so the first paper starts higher on the page. “Scope & authors” / “研究范围与作者” opens the scope and limitations, authors, original title and BibTeX link in a native disclosure. Under it, a counted link such as “3 sources · checked 2026-10-16 →” / “3 个来源 · 复核于 2026-10-16 →” opens the entry page's `#entry-sources` list; it counts each distinct source once, as the entry page lists them, and its accessible name includes the paper title. The primary sources, “Why it fits”, publication and first arXiv dates and their basis, DOI and arXiv identifiers, the reviewed arXiv version and the review notes appear only on the entry pages, which keeps the listings light; `validate_site.py` checks that each entry page has them. `?layout=cards` (carried by the language link) switches to cards and brings scope into view. Search reads a content-addressed index, `/assets/paper-search-index.<SHA-256 prefix>.json`, which both languages share: each listing names it in the search form's `data-search-index` and preloads it with `as="fetch" crossorigin`, the request [paper-search.js](../site/paper-search.js) makes, so it downloads while the page parses and is then cached like the scripts. It holds only the fields search reads (`SEARCH_FIELDS` in build_paper_pages.py): both titles and summaries, authors, venue, DOI, arXiv ID, year, status and targets. The layout applies before the index arrives; anything typed meanwhile is kept and applied when it does, and if the request fails the inert search form is hidden. `validate_site.py` checks the preload, the file name against its content and the index against the listed cards, and prints both listings' sizes; above the advisory 900,000-byte `LISTING_SIZE_BUDGET` it prints a warning without failing, so data pull requests keep passing. [test_paper_listing_size.py](../tests/test_paper_listing_size.py) builds the 206 papers listed when the budget was set and fails if either listing reaches it. Existing `?layout=compact` links remain supported. The automated repository index continues to use category pages and does not generate individual pages for scanned repositories.
- Every generated page whose header has a language link (repository directory, collection, paper, survey and detail pages) loads [language-fragment.js](../site/language-fragment.js); [language_fragment.py](../scripts/language_fragment.py) adds it after the page builders run. Both language versions of a page share their card and section IDs, so when the current fragment names an element on the page, the language link carries it to the same card or section. Unknown or malformed fragments are dropped and links to another origin are never rewritten; without JavaScript the link opens the top of the counterpart page. The homepages keep their fragment through app.js.
- [agent_formats.py](../scripts/agent_formats.py) renders the Markdown twin (`index.md`) of each entry, listing and category page and the bilingual `record.json` of each entry, plus `llms-full.txt`; `alternate_links()` writes the `<link rel="alternate">` tags a page uses to advertise them, and new page templates should call it the same way. [build_api.py](../scripts/build_api.py) writes `/api/v1/` and the `/api/` documentation page, which uses the `/about/` page template. [validate_agent_formats.py](../scripts/validate_agent_formats.py), called by `validate_site.py`, checks that every promised twin is linked and matches its record, that every API file follows `schema.json` (checked by [json_schema_check.py](../scripts/json_schema_check.py)) and the catalog, that the JSON Feeds repeat the Atom feeds, that `llms.txt` stays under 50 KB with working links, and that `_headers` serves these formats.
- [page_twins.py](../scripts/page_twins.py) gives every indexed page that no builder writes a twin for, such as the homepages, the survey, `/about/` and `/contribute/`, an `index.md` converted from its `<main>` and the `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` that announces it.
- [validate_discovery.py](../scripts/validate_discovery.py) checks the generated site's canonical routes, language links, static record coverage, JSON-LD and crawler permissions. The production build and CI both run it. See [search discovery](search-discovery.md) for sources, submission steps, and measurement limits.
- `dist/` is ignored by Git. Rebuild it from source instead of editing generated files. The resource count is a count of catalog records, not distinct software projects.
- Builds generate a fresh site in ignored `.cache/` storage before replacing `dist/`, so removed source assets do not survive a rebuild. A generation or manifest failure leaves the previous output intact. If replacement fails, the builder restores the previous directory; if restoration also fails, it reports the retained recovery directory. Treat all files inside `dist/` as generated output, not a place for unrelated files.

## Build and preview

Run from the repository root with Python 3.10+ and Node.js available:

```sh
python3 scripts/validate.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/build_site.py
node --check site/app.js
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory dist
```

The test command runs every Python test and the Node tests of the browser scripts offline; CI runs the same discovered tests split across its four `unit` shards. The [browser smoke test](#browser-smoke-test) is a separate step.

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Use HTTP rather than opening `index.html` directly, because the directory fetches `catalog-index.json`, `catalog.json` and `source-browser.json`. Stop the preview server with Ctrl+C.

After source, locale, scope, curated-record or paper edits, regenerate the [GitHub browsing directory](repositories/README.md) with `python3 scripts/build_repository_index.py` before validation. It also updates the counts and directory links in both root READMEs. A repository line whose exact GitHub repository is a curated entry's URL or a paper's code or project URL ends with a “Curated” or “Paper” link to that page, using the same matching as the website's related links; `--check` fails when these markers are stale.

The bare homepage always opens in English. Use `/zh/` or the header language links to open Chinese; old browser preferences do not override the default. Generated pages link to `/zh/` routes, while existing `?lang=zh` links still render Chinese.

Before publication, check English and Chinese at desktop and 390 px widths: search, all filter types, empty results, clearing filters, loading more, prerequisite expansion, keyboard focus and the language links. Confirm repository descriptions change language alongside the interface, including filtered and newly loaded cards. Check translated prerequisites and empty-description fallbacks, and confirm the canonical URL, social image URLs, `CNAME`, robots and sitemap agree on `awesomerea.org`. The browser smoke test below automates part of this list; it does not replace the review.

Printing follows one policy, set in the `@media print` block of [styles.css](../site/styles.css) (the survey keeps its own print styles). Static pages print as plain documents: navigation, search, filters, category and topic links and page actions are left out, the header is no longer sticky, cards print without shadows and in one column, headings stay with their text, and long URLs, DOIs and hashes wrap. Listing pages (`/resources/`, `/cases/`, `/browse/` and `/papers/`) print every entry's visible text plus any disclosure the reader opened; on `/resources/` and `/cases/` that text includes the primary source and the counted link to the entry page's requirements and sources, and on `/papers/` the counted link to the entry page's sources with their review date. Closed requirement and source disclosures are left out, except that each paper always prints its scope and limitations and the review notes (“About this index”, “About these cases”) always print. A print-only line under the listing heading states this in the page's language. Detail pages have no disclosures, so they print every requirement, limitation and source. Title, source and paper links print their address after the link text. Revealing closed disclosures uses `::details-content`; in a browser without it, the review notes and paper scope stay collapsed as on screen. Check print previews in both languages after changing card markup.

The validators derive the sitemap inventory from collection routes, category definitions and current curated/paper IDs. Adding or removing a reviewed entry changes two detail URLs; there is no fixed page-count limit. Checks require exact detail IDs, complete localized content, ordinary listing links, reciprocal languages, self-canonicals and source-bound structured data. The entry builder removes only obsolete pages carrying its own generated-page marker and preserves listing pages and citation downloads.

Review the exact `dist/` payload for credentials, account identifiers, administrative URLs, personal filesystem paths and unrelated files. The public catalog should contain public source links only. Publish generated assets, never an entire working directory or `.git` folder. `source-reviewed` describes a check of the resource's documentation; it does not assert that every listed tool has been executed.

### Browser smoke test

[smoke.cjs](../tests/browser/smoke.cjs) rebuilds `dist/` with the public fallback icons, serves it on `127.0.0.1` with the [site/_headers](../site/_headers) rules, and loads it in an installed headless Chrome or Chromium at 1280 px and 390 px. Requests to any other origin are blocked. Both homepages and a set of collection, about, browse and detail pages must load without console errors, Content Security Policy violations, failed local requests or horizontal page overflow. On `/resources/` and `/cases/` in both languages, each target section's count line must add up to the cards in that section and stay inside the viewport. On each homepage it also checks the initial curated and repository card counts and status totals against the built JSON, a search-and-clear cycle, Show More in both views, requirement expansion, and a language switch that keeps a target filter and the fragment. It also checks that the catalog arrives through its preload in one request while `source-browser.json` waits for the Repositories view, and that arrow keys on the language links never navigate. On `/papers/` and `/zh/papers/` it checks each row's counted sources link, that the search index arrives through its preload in one request, and a typed search for one paper's ID. With JavaScript disabled, both homepages must show no search or filter controls and no loading text, with the static directory links under the collection heading.

```sh
npm ci --prefix tests/browser --ignore-scripts
node tests/browser/smoke.cjs
```

The pinned `puppeteer-core` package drives the installed browser and downloads none; set `CHROME_PATH` when Chrome is not in a standard location. Without a browser or the package, the test prints the reason and skips locally, while CI fails. Screenshots are written to the ignored `.cache/browser-smoke/` directory, and CI keeps them as the `browser-smoke-screenshots` workflow artifact for 14 days. They are for people to inspect: the test does not compare images, approve the visual design, or open any linked resource.

### Fonts and icons

The site self-hosts its fonts in [site/fonts](../site/fonts): subsets of EB Garamond, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono under the SIL Open Font License ([site/fonts/LICENSE.md](../site/fonts/LICENSE.md)). `scripts/review_pr.py` accepts exactly these files. Icons are inline SVG, so no icon font or third-party asset origin is involved. `--fontawesome-assets-url` is still accepted and ignored, for build commands configured outside this repository.

## Hosting

GitHub Pages publishes the website. The `publish.yml` workflows in `Awesome-REA/awesomerea.org` and `Awesome-REA/awesome-rea.com` check out this repository's `main`, run `scripts/build_production.py --publish`, write the commit to `/source-commit.txt` and deploy `dist/` without `_headers` and `_redirects`. Both domains are proxied through Cloudflare. Keep this collection's source public; `Awesome-REA/awesome-rea.github.io` is reserved for **private artifact backups**, independently of the hosting service. Confirm its visibility when maintaining that backup. GitHub Free for organizations supports Pages from public repositories; private-repository Pages requires a qualifying paid plan. [GitHub Pages availability](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages).

Each workflow runs twice an hour (at :27 and :57 for awesomerea.org, :12 and :42 for awesome-rea.com) and on manual dispatch, and publishes when its domain serves a commit other than the head of `main`. The Cloudflare Cache Rule **Cache static site HTML at the edge for 30 minutes** keeps every response at the edge for 30 minutes, so a new build reaches visitors once the zone's cache is purged after the deployment. `curl https://awesomerea.org/source-commit.txt` shows the commit a domain serves.

The canonical host is `awesomerea.org`. The Cloudflare Single Redirect named **Canonical www to apex** matches `(http.host eq "www.awesomerea.org")` and returns **301** with the dynamic target `concat("https://awesomerea.org", http.request.uri.path)` and **Preserve query string** enabled. Keep the existing `www` DNS record proxied so the rule runs. This hostname rule is configured at the Cloudflare edge; Pages `_redirects` does not support host matching. [Single Redirects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/rules/url-forwarding/single-redirects/), [Pages domain redirect guidance](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/how-to/www-redirect/).

Include these checks after deployment or domain changes:

```sh
curl --head --silent 'https://www.awesomerea.org/papers/?x=1'
curl --location --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{num_redirects}\n' 'http://www.awesomerea.org/'
```

The first request should return `301` and `location: https://awesomerea.org/papers/?x=1`. The second should end at `https://awesomerea.org/` with `200` in at most two redirects. Also check a localized path and repeated or encoded query parameters, and confirm the corresponding apex page still returns `200` without a hostname redirect.

GitHub Pages does not read [site/_headers](../site/_headers); Cloudflare sends its headers. In each zone the Response Header Transform Rule **Security headers from site/_headers (/\*), without HSTS** sets the `/*` block's Content Security Policy, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, Permissions Policy that disables unused device features and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` on every response, together with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Its values are copied from `site/_headers` at the published commit when a build is published, so `_headers` remains the place to change them. The `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=2592000` line in `_headers` is not sent. External links use `rel="noopener"` without `noreferrer`, both in generated pages and in links built by app.js, so a linked project, and this repository's GitHub traffic view, can see that a visit came from `https://awesomerea.org/`, but never the page path or the `?q=` search text. `validate_site.py` requires the policy, rejects `noreferrer`, and requires `noopener` on every new-tab link. The policy allows only same-origin scripts, styles, fonts, images, JSON requests and form submissions; `validate_site.py` fails the build if a page adds inline code, inline styles, frames or another asset origin. Form submissions are allowed only for the GET search on the two 404 pages. The host serves the 404 page under the missing path, so only the `/*` policy reaches it, and a second policy could only narrow it; `validate_site.py` therefore requires `form-action 'self'` with no other source and fails if any other page has a form with an `action` or `method`. The paper search is handled by script and never submits. Cloudflare's same-origin email-decoding script is allowed, and so is Cloudflare Web Analytics, which the edge injects only on the production domain (its beacon from `https://static.cloudflareinsights.com` and its reports to `https://cloudflareinsights.com`); `validate_site.py` keeps both origins in the policy because built pages never show the beacon. Enabling Zaraz, JavaScript detections or any other injected script requires updating the policy first. Sending HSTS, with or without `includeSubDomains` and `preload`, needs an owner decision about every subdomain.

Every page links its stylesheets and scripts at content-addressed `/assets/<name>.<SHA-256 prefix>.css` or `.js` paths written by [asset_paths.py](../scripts/asset_paths.py); a changed file always gets a new name. The Transform Rule **Year-long cache for content-addressed /assets/ files** sends the `/assets/*` value from `_headers`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, on successful `/assets/` responses, and the Cache Rule **Year-long edge cache for content-addressed /assets/ files; errors for 60 s** keeps those files at the edge for a year. The paper search index is the one generated data file there: `/assets/paper-search-index.<SHA-256 prefix>.json`. HTML, `catalog.json`, `papers.json`, the source-index files and the manifests are sent with GitHub Pages' `Cache-Control: max-age=600`; their `no-cache` rules in `_headers` apply in the browser smoke test. `validate_site.py` fails if a page links an unhashed same-origin stylesheet or script, if a file name, including a preloaded `/assets/` file's, does not match its content, if a stylesheet or script remains outside `/assets/`, or if any other rule is immutable.

Two absolute-URL rules in the same file add `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` to `https://:project.pages.dev/*` and `https://:version.:project.pages.dev/*`, so a project's `pages.dev` alias, its preview and branch deployments, and any Direct Upload of this build stay out of search results. They never match `awesomerea.org`, and `validate_site.py` fails if any path rule would send that header to the canonical host. [Cloudflare Pages headers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/headers/).

## Direct Upload for the icon origin or a manual deployment

Build first. Cloudflare accepts a folder or ZIP through drag and drop; Wrangler accepts the asset folder. Direct Upload is a different project mode from Git integration. [Official Direct Upload instructions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/get-started/direct-upload/).

To create a ZIP whose `index.html` is at the archive root:

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import shutil

Path(".cache").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
shutil.make_archive(".cache/awesomerea-site", "zip", "dist")
PY
```

An authorized maintainer can open the intended Pages Direct Upload project, create a production deployment, and upload `.cache/awesomerea-site.zip` or the `dist/` folder. Do not wrap the assets in an extra `dist/` directory inside the ZIP. Alternatively, use an authenticated Wrangler session and select the intended project:

```sh
npx wrangler pages deploy dist
```

After deployment, verify the returned deployment URL, then confirm the custom-domain and DNS configuration for `awesomerea.org`. A generated `CNAME` file or a successful local build does not establish hosting, DNS or TLS status. Keep hosting credentials outside the repository; only the approved static artifacts belong in the optional backup repository.


## Homepage and explorer

`/` and `/zh/` come from [build_home.py](../scripts/build_home.py): the masthead, search and the index-card drawer on curated data, with counts from the records and the scan-only discovery count labelled as unreviewed. Without JavaScript the tabs and cards are links and the search form opens the listing; [site.js](../site/site.js) adds in-place search from `/search-index.json` or `/search-index.zh.json`, loaded on first use. Every generated page shares the header, command palette and theme from [site_shell.py](../scripts/site_shell.py) and [shell.css](../site/shell.css), and the footer from [site_footer.py](../scripts/site_footer.py). The footer's last-scan cell is filled at runtime from `/discoveries/status.json`, so a scan does not change every page's bytes.

The earlier interactive collection, with its filters, repository view and shortlist, is kept at `/explore/` and `/zh/explore/` (noindex, out of the sitemap). Its old query links redirect there from the homepage. The next paragraphs describe that page where they mention filters, cards or the collection heading.

## Homepage languages and discovery

The build writes an English homepage at `/` and a complete Chinese homepage at `/zh/`. Each has its own canonical URL, localized title and description, and reciprocal `hreflang` links. Both routes appear in the sitemap. The header shows an English / 简体中文 link pair inside a group with a localized name; the current language has `aria-current="true"`. The build points each link at its own homepage, so switching works without JavaScript, and app.js keeps both links in step with the query, layout and fragment whenever the URL changes. Arrow keys never navigate. Existing `?lang=zh` links remain readable; the language links drop `lang`, because the path selects the language.

Each view's results line (`#results-status`, `#source-status`) is a polite live region whose text is replaced only when it changes, so it announces the matching count after a search or filter change but not again when Show More reveals another page. Show More instead fills a separate visually hidden live region after its row (`#more-status`, `#source-more-status`) with the number added and the number now shown out of the total, for example “15 more resources shown: 30 of 225.” / “又显示 15 项资源，已显示 30 / 225 项。”. That message clears on any other change, and focus still moves to the first newly revealed card.

Homepage navigation and featured collection links are ordinary HTML links, available before JavaScript runs. Without scripting, `@media (scripting: none)` hides the search field, filters, selects, tabs and layout control, and the status lines start empty; the noscript note under the collection heading links the static repository directory, curated collection and papers instead. Each homepage preloads `/catalog-index.json?v=<data revision>` with `as="fetch" crossorigin`, the exact request app.js makes, so the index downloads while the page parses; `validate_site.py` fails if the preload and `data-catalog-revision` diverge. The index holds only the fields the first render needs (`CATALOG_INDEX_FIELDS` in build_site.py), and `validate_site.py` checks that it projects `catalog.json` record for record. Right after the first render app.js fetches the complete `catalog.json` once: open details show “Loading requirements…” until it arrives and are then filled in place, and a query is re-run so it also matches requirement text. If that request fails, typing a query or reopening details retries it. `catalog.json` remains the complete download. `source-browser.json` is not preloaded and loads only with the Repositories view. Search uses the curated catalog by default; `?view=source-index` explicitly opens the automated repository index. Both views share the contributor credits. Choosing a collection, a target, Type, Category, either Sort control or a topic chip, and Clear or Reset, adds a browser history entry; typing in either search field or the topic field and changing the layout replace the current entry instead. Back and Forward restore the collection, language, query, filters, sort order and layout from the address without adding entries, apply the same safe defaults as a shared link, and leave the results, Show More progress and open details alone when only the fragment differs. Font Awesome Pro continues to load through the configured authorized asset origin; no licensed font binaries are committed.

Readers can keep an optional shortlist in their own browser. Curated and repository cards on the homepage and paper cards on `/papers/` have a Save toggle (`aria-pressed`, with the entry name in its accessible name). Saving stores only `type:id` keys (`curated:`, `repository:` or `paper:` plus the stable ID) under the `awesomerea-shortlist` localStorage key; app.js and [paper-search.js](../site/paper-search.js) share that format and no request carries it. Once something is saved, the homepage shows a Shortlist button with the saved count and the paper directory a Shortlist link (`/#shortlist`); both open a dialog that resolves each key against the homepage's own `catalog-index.json` load (it adds no catalog request of its own and fills in once that load settles), the repository browser data or `papers.json`, lists curated entries and papers with their detail pages and repositories with their upstream links, and offers Remove and Clear shortlist. An ID that is no longer listed stays visible as unavailable instead of matching another entry, and data that fails to load keeps the saved ID. Without usable localStorage the toggles and Shortlist controls are not shown; a failed write is announced and leaves the list unchanged. There is no account or synchronization.

Search in both views also covers text a card does not show: the other language's name and description, requirements, the original upstream description, topics, related-entry titles and category, type, relationship and target labels. Curated search also matches the lowercase GitHub owner/repo of each entry's URL and, when it names another repository, of its primary source, so `zeldaret` or `x64dbg/x64dbg` finds the entries hosted there; only the owner/repo is added, never a host, file path, fragment or non-GitHub address. When a query term is absent from a card's visible title, description and labels, a “Matched in” line under the description names the field that holds it (at most two fields, such as “GitHub repository” for a path-only curated match) and quotes a short excerpt with the term marked. It folds text the same way as the search index (NFKC and lower case), so full-width text and queries are marked too. Requirement matches appear once the complete `catalog.json` has loaded and the query is re-run. It never replaces the displayed translation or fills an empty description, inserts the excerpt as text, cuts it on whole characters and leaves result order and focus unchanged.

Activating a repository topic chip from the keyboard moves focus to the Topic field, which now shows that topic, because the re-rendered list replaces the chip. Clear filters in either view and the repository Reset filters button hide themselves once used, so keyboard activation returns focus to that collection's search field; the curated empty-state Reset filters always did. Pointer clicks keep the browser's default, so touch screens do not open a keyboard, and Show More still focuses the first newly shown entry.

When a nonblank curated query has no matches, readers can continue with the same query in the active language's paper directory or the available repository index. The paper link opens the existing bibliography search; the repository action retains its automatic-index label. Offering these actions does not fetch either collection or promise a match.

Each collection's results line has an “Export matches (JSON)” / “导出匹配项（JSON）” button. It downloads every current match in the displayed order, including results Show More has not revealed, as `awesomerea-curated-matches.json` or `awesomerea-repository-matches.json`. An `export` header names the collection, record class, filters, page URL, data revision and full download; repository exports also copy the scan snapshot and state that the records are automatic README observations, not curated entries. Records are copied unchanged without the browser's search fields, so curated entries keep their own source review and repositories excluded from browsing stay out. Curated exports copy the complete `catalog.json` records rather than the lean `catalog-index.json` the cards render from, and wait for that file if it has not loaded yet. A status line under the results reports the download, an empty result or a browser that cannot create the file; the footer's full JSON downloads are unchanged.

Each curated target button and each Type and Category option shows how many resources it would return with the other active filters and the current query, and choices that would return none are disabled unless they are the current selection, so shared URLs still show their own choice. The counts update while typing and are not announced; the results status remains the only live region. The build writes the unfiltered target counts into both homepages and shows the Protocol button there when a curated record has that target, so the filter row does not move when app.js first renders. The interactive catalog defaults to a compact list. The Layout control switches between compact rows and cards without rebuilding results, so expanded details and current filters stay in place. `?layout=cards` shares the card layout; omitting it uses the compact list. The choice travels with language links. Compact curated rows name each entry's targets before its category at every width, wrapping on narrow screens. Compact repository rows keep related entries and clickable topics inside Details; descriptions remain complete at the same reading size. Below 700 px both layouts are one column, so the Layout control is hidden (a shared `?layout=` still applies); Type and Category fold behind a “More filters” button that counts active selects and starts open when the page loads filtered, and the review note follows the results. Show More appends the next 15 curated or 24 repository cards after the ones already shown and moves focus to the first new card, so each click costs the same however far a reader has gone. A search or filter change rebuilds the list from the first page and a language change rebuilds the cards already shown; both keep open details that remain visible.

Curated results default to the featured entries, then kind and catalog order. With a nonblank query, that default order (“Featured first”) still keeps every record that contains each term but ranks the matches by where the terms occur: English or Chinese names first, then descriptions, then category, type, relationship and target labels, then requirement text, with a match at a word start above one inside a word. A query that is an entry's whole name, ignoring spaces and punctuation, leads, and featured order, kind and catalog order break ties. Requirement text counts once the complete `catalog.json` has loaded. The Sort control beside the result count can instead order every match, including those Show More reveals, by name or by latest source review. Name order compares the active language's displayed names with that language's collator and breaks ties by record ID, so switching language can reorder the same matches but never changes which records match. Source-review order uses the displayed `verified_at` date, newest first, and keeps the default order within a day; it reflects when the catalog checked the source, not upstream activity. `?order=name` and `?order=reviewed` share the choice, an unknown value falls back to the default, and Clear filters keeps the order, like the layout. Curated exports follow the chosen order and name it as `order` among the export's filters.

Under each collection's result count, every active constraint appears as a chip naming its field and value: the query, target, Type, Category and a shared `?group=` in the curated view, and the query, target and topic in the repository view. Valid filters without a visible control, such as a Protocol target whose button is hidden, still get a chip, including when nothing matches. Each chip is a button whose accessible name says which filter it removes; removing one adds a history entry like Clear filters, keeps the other filters, language, layout and sort order, and moves focus to the chip that takes its place, the previous chip or, when none remain, the collection's search field. Clear filters still resets everything.
